request_payload.input: I want to compare two English-to-German systems on held-out online news from late 2019. Which public test set and scoring setup should I use?
request_payload.instructions: Answer the research question from existing knowledge. Aim for 180–240 words and do not exceed 300 words. Do not browse or use external tools. Do not ask a follow-up question.

output_text: Use the WMT20 English–German General MT test set, often distributed as newstest2020 or wmt20-en-de. It is a public, held-out test set built from recent news material and is the standard choice for comparing English-to-German MT systems on late-2019 online news. Download the official source and reference files from the WMT20 General MT task page, and use the same references for both systems. For scoring, use sacreBLEU with the official WMT20 configuration: 13a tokenization and case-sensitive scoring. Do not add extra normalization, detokenization, or language-specific post-editing before scoring unless you apply it identically to both systems. Report the sacreBLEU score as the primary metric; if you want additional diagnostics, you can also report chrF or TER, but keep sacreBLEU as the comparison metric. This setup is reproducible, widely used, and directly comparable with published WMT20 results. If your systems are neural MT systems, ensure that both use the same decoding parameters, vocabulary, and inference preprocessing, then score the raw hypothesis outputs against the WMT20 EN-DE reference. Because the set is held out from the public WMT training data, it reduces the risk that models have memorized the evaluation sentences. It is also small enough for fast comparison but large enough to produce stable differences between strong systems. If you need an even more recent or domain-specific news set, WMT21 or WMT22 EN-DE test sets are alternatives, but WMT20 best matches your late-2019 online-news requirement.
